articles.summary:
Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections

US president Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran... will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," he wrote in a post on his platform Truth Social. 

Trump added that Iran "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but claimed that the attacks have "all been knocked down, and done no damage".

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won’t let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," the American president further claimed. 

Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange".

In another post, he questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"

South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran

South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said that a motion to extend the deployment of the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit in the Gulf of Aden did not amount to involvement in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The minister told lawmakers that the deployment was not indirect military participation in the conflict, but instead cited a rise in piracy alongside efforts to protect South Korean ships and citizens using the maritime route.

articles.title: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
articles.summary:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?

Turkey's foreign minister has warned that Israel could launch a military operation in Syria, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention.

Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials.

"There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said.

The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis.

Read more: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?

articles.title: Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
articles.summary:
Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages

Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank have described how Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and sprayed racist graffiti on homes during overnight attacks on several villages.

Footage from Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik on Sunday shows burnt-out cars and graffiti reading "Death to Arabs" and "Revenge" painted on walls. Residents said settlers attacked their villages while families were asleep, leaving multiple vehicles destroyed.

"We were sleeping and not expecting that herds of settlers will attack our homes while people are sleeping, we never expected this," said Muneer Alkhatib, a resident of Deir Abu Mashal.

Another resident, Montaser Almalki, said the attackers came from a nearby settler outpost and warned that his family could have been caught in a fire had they not woken up.

The attacks took place across several locations in the occupied West Bank. They were condemned by Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who described them as "Jewish terrorism" and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for encouraging the violence.

articles.summary: Three Palestinians were killed and four others, including a child, were injured in Israeli attacks in the Gaza Strip, in the latest violation of last year’s ceasefire agreement, medical sources said, Anadolu Agency. articles.title: Landmine explosion kills 4 children, injures 2 in northwestern Syria
articles.summary: Four children were killed and two others injured on Sunday when a landmine exploded in Syria’s northwestern Idlib province, Alikhbaria TV reported. Citing its correspondent, the broadcaster said the mine was left behind by the ousted regime of Bashar al-Assad and exploded in the village of Umm Khazim in rural Idlib. It gave no further details on the circumstances of the blast or the condition of the injured children. Landmines and unexploded ordnance continue to kill and injure people across Syria. Syrian authorities and international organizations are working in several parts of the country to locate and clear them.
